# Requires only: make, bash, docker, docker compose v2.
SHELL := bash
.DEFAULT_GOAL := help

FRONTEND_PORT ?= 8080
export FRONTEND_PORT

COMPOSE := docker compose
# The test stack is a separate compose project (own containers, network and
# volume) built from the base file only, so it publishes no host ports and
# never touches the data of a running `make up` stack.
TEST_COMPOSE := docker compose -p job-dashboard-test -f docker-compose.yml --profile e2e

.PHONY: help build up test stop clean

help: ## Show this help
	@grep -E '^[a-z-]+:.*## ' $(MAKEFILE_LIST) | awk -F ':.*## ' '{printf "  make %-8s %s\n", $$1, $$2}'

build: ## Build the Docker images
	$(COMPOSE) build

up: ## Start the app at http://localhost:8080 (override: FRONTEND_PORT=3000 make up)
	$(COMPOSE) up -d --build --wait
	@echo "App running at http://localhost:$(FRONTEND_PORT)"

# One shell invocation so the trap always tears the stack down and the recipe
# exits with the Playwright exit code. A leftover stack from an interrupted run
# is removed first, so every run starts from an empty database. If startup or a
# test fails, the service logs are printed before the stack is removed.
test: ## Run the Playwright E2E tests against a fresh, isolated stack
	@trap '$(TEST_COMPOSE) down -v --remove-orphans' EXIT; \
	dump_logs() { echo "--- service logs (last 200 lines each) ---"; $(TEST_COMPOSE) logs --no-color --tail 200 db backend frontend; }; \
	$(TEST_COMPOSE) down -v --remove-orphans && \
	$(TEST_COMPOSE) build && \
	{ $(TEST_COMPOSE) up -d --wait db backend frontend || { dump_logs; exit 1; }; } && \
	{ $(TEST_COMPOSE) run --rm -T e2e || { status=$$?; dump_logs; exit $$status; }; }

stop: ## Stop the running containers (data is kept)
	$(COMPOSE) stop

clean: ## Remove containers, networks and volumes of the app and test stacks
	$(COMPOSE) down -v --remove-orphans
	$(TEST_COMPOSE) down -v --remove-orphans
# The application stack. No host ports are published here: `make up` adds them
# from docker-compose.override.yml (loaded automatically), while `make test`
# loads only this file, so a busy port on the host cannot fail the tests.
name: job-dashboard

services:
  db:
    image: postgres:17-alpine
    environment:
      POSTGRES_DB: ${POSTGRES_DB:-jobs}
      POSTGRES_USER: ${POSTGRES_USER:-jobs}
      # Development default. The database is reachable only inside the compose
      # network; a real deployment supplies its own value.
      POSTGRES_PASSWORD: ${POSTGRES_PASSWORD:-jobs}
    volumes:
      - db-data:/var/lib/postgresql/data
    healthcheck:
      # -h 127.0.0.1 checks over TCP. On first start the image runs a temporary
      # server on the unix socket only; a socket check would pass too early.
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "pg_isready -h 127.0.0.1 -U \"$$POSTGRES_USER\" -d \"$$POSTGRES_DB\""]
      interval: 2s
      timeout: 3s
      retries: 30

  backend:
    build: ./backend
    environment:
      POSTGRES_DB: ${POSTGRES_DB:-jobs}
      POSTGRES_USER: ${POSTGRES_USER:-jobs}
      POSTGRES_PASSWORD: ${POSTGRES_PASSWORD:-jobs}
      POSTGRES_HOST: db
      # Any Host header is accepted so the app also works when opened by IP or
      # hostname on a remote machine. Acceptable only because nothing here
      # builds emails, caches responses or authenticates users. settings.py
      # keeps a strict default for anything not started through this file.
      # TODO: before adding auth, set this to the real hostname(s).
      DJANGO_ALLOWED_HOSTS: ${DJANGO_ALLOWED_HOSTS:-*}
      DJANGO_SECRET_KEY: ${DJANGO_SECRET_KEY:-insecure-dev-only-key}
    depends_on:
      db:
        condition: service_healthy
    healthcheck:
      # The slim Python image has no curl, so the check uses Python itself.
      test: ["CMD", "python", "-c", "import urllib.request; urllib.request.urlopen('http://127.0.0.1:8000/api/health/', timeout=2)"]
      interval: 2s
      timeout: 3s
      retries: 30

  frontend:
    build: ./frontend
    depends_on:
      backend:
        condition: service_healthy
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD", "wget", "-q", "--spider", "http://127.0.0.1/"]
      interval: 2s
      timeout: 3s
      retries: 30

  # Playwright runner. Behind a profile so `make up` never builds or starts it.
  e2e:
    profiles: [e2e]
    build: ./e2e
    environment:
      BASE_URL: http://frontend
    depends_on:
      frontend:
        condition: service_healthy
    # Chromium needs more shared memory than Docker's 64 MB default, and an
    # init process to reap the helper processes it spawns.
    shm_size: 1gb
    init: true
    # TODO: traces of failed tests stay inside the container and are removed
    # with it. Deferred: a bind mount would leave root-owned files in the clone
    # on Linux. Fix: `docker compose cp` the test-results folder out on failure.

volumes:

# Local-run additions, merged automatically by `docker compose` / `make up`.
# Not used by `make test`.
services:

    ports:
      - "${FRONTEND_PORT:-8080}:80"

import logging

from django.db import Error as DatabaseError
from django.db import connection
from django.http import HttpRequest, JsonResponse
from django.views.decorators.http import require_GET

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)


@require_GET
def health(request: HttpRequest) -> JsonResponse:
    """Report whether this process can reach the database.

    Used by the container healthcheck, so it must stay cheap.

    :param request: The incoming GET request; its content is not used.
    :returns: 200 ``{"status": "ok"}`` when ``SELECT 1`` succeeds, otherwise
        503 ``{"status": "unavailable"}``.
    """
    try:
        with connection.cursor() as cursor:
            cursor.execute("SELECT 1")
    except DatabaseError:
        logger.exception("Health check failed: database unreachable")
        return JsonResponse({"status": "unavailable"}, status=503)
    return JsonResponse({"status": "ok"})

content.text:
**The issue, simply.** "When a job is deleted, delete its statuses" can be enforced by one of two parties:

- **The app (ORM cascade).** Django sees `on_delete=CASCADE` and itself runs two statements in one transaction: `DELETE FROM jobs_jobstatus WHERE job_id = 7`, then `DELETE FROM jobs_job WHERE id = 7`. The database only has a plain foreign key, with no `ON DELETE` clause.
- **The database (`ON DELETE CASCADE`).** The rule is part of the FK constraint. Anyone who deletes a job, by any route, has its statuses removed by Postgres.

In your stack this is the same split as SQLAlchemy's `relationship(cascade="all, delete-orphan")` (app-side) versus `ForeignKey(..., ondelete="CASCADE")` (in the MySQL DDL). Django 5.2 only offers the first; it never writes `ON DELETE CASCADE` into the schema.

That means the Phase 2 manual check in CLAUDE.md ("confirm the FK `ON DELETE` behaviour exists in the database itself") cannot pass as written: `\d jobs_jobstatus` will show the FK with no `ON DELETE` clause.

**What happens in each case**

| | ORM cascade | DB-level `ON DELETE CASCADE` |
|---|---|---|
| `DELETE /api/jobs/<id>/` (the spec requirement) | Works: statuses then job, one transaction | Works |
| Raw SQL `DELETE FROM jobs_job` in psql or a script | Refused with an FK error if statuses exist; nothing is orphaned | Statuses silently deleted too |
| How it is built | One model argument; migration fully auto-generated | Extra hand-written `RunSQL` migration that drops and re-creates the constraint |
| Schema vs models | Identical | Database has a rule Django's model state does not know about; a later change to that FK can silently drop it |
| Cost per delete | 2 statements, the first using the auto-created `job_id` index | 1 statement, same index |
| Walkthrough | Standard Django, nothing to explain | You must explain the raw SQL and why it does not match the model |

**Recommendation: ORM cascade.** It meets the spec, the app is the only writer, and the failure mode for a raw delete is a loud error rather than orphaned rows. The DB-level version buys protection for a route (raw SQL deletes) that this project does not have, at the price of hand-maintained SQL. I would add a `TODO` on the FK noting the gap and correct the manual check wording to "FK exists, with an index on `job_id`; cascade is done by Django".

      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "pg_isready -h 127.0.0.1 -U \"$$POSTGRES_USER\" -d \"$$POSTGRES_DB\""]

"""Model tests: what the database itself guarantees for Job and JobStatus.

They run against real Postgres with the real migration applied, so a passing
test means the constraint exists in the schema, not only in Python.
"""
from datetime import datetime, timedelta, timezone as dt_timezone
from unittest import mock

import pytest
from django.core.management import call_command
from django.db import DataError, IntegrityError, transaction
from django.utils import timezone

from jobs.models import Job, JobStatus, StatusType

pytestmark = pytest.mark.django_db

T0 = datetime(2026, 1, 1, 12, 0, tzinfo=dt_timezone.utc)
T1 = T0 + timedelta(hours=1)


def test_status_type_has_the_four_states() -> None:
    assert StatusType.values == ["PENDING", "RUNNING", "COMPLETED", "FAILED"]


def test_create_sets_both_timestamps() -> None:
    with mock.patch("django.utils.timezone.now", return_value=T0):
        job = Job.objects.create(name="Fluid Dynamics Simulation")

    job.refresh_from_db()
    assert job.created_at == T0
    assert job.updated_at == T0


def test_save_moves_updated_at_and_keeps_created_at() -> None:
    with mock.patch("django.utils.timezone.now", return_value=T0):
        job = Job.objects.create(name="ML Model Training")

    with mock.patch("django.utils.timezone.now", return_value=T1):
        job.save()

    job.refresh_from_db()
    assert job.created_at == T0
    assert job.updated_at == T1


def test_new_job_defaults_to_pending() -> None:
    job = Job.objects.create(name="job")

    job.refresh_from_db()
    assert job.current_status == StatusType.PENDING


@pytest.mark.parametrize("status", ["BOGUS", "pending", ""])
def test_database_rejects_invalid_job_current_status(status: str) -> None:
    # atomic() gives the failing INSERT its own savepoint, so the error does
    # not poison the transaction the test itself runs in.
    with pytest.raises(IntegrityError), transaction.atomic():
        Job.objects.create(name="job", current_status=status)

    assert not Job.objects.exists()


@pytest.mark.parametrize("status", ["BOGUS", "pending", ""])
def test_database_rejects_invalid_jobstatus_status_type(status: str) -> None:
    job = Job.objects.create(name="job")

    with pytest.raises(IntegrityError), transaction.atomic():
        JobStatus.objects.create(job=job, status_type=status)

    assert not JobStatus.objects.exists()


@pytest.mark.parametrize("name", ["", " ", "\t\n  "])
def test_database_rejects_blank_job_name(name: str) -> None:
    with pytest.raises(IntegrityError), transaction.atomic():
        Job.objects.create(name=name)

    assert not Job.objects.exists()


def test_job_name_accepts_255_characters_and_rejects_256() -> None:
    Job.objects.create(name="x" * 255)

    with pytest.raises(DataError), transaction.atomic():
        Job.objects.create(name="x" * 256)

    assert Job.objects.count() == 1


def test_jobstatus_timestamp_defaults_to_now() -> None:
    job = Job.objects.create(name="job")

    before = timezone.now()
    status = JobStatus.objects.create(job=job, status_type=StatusType.PENDING)
    after = timezone.now()

    status.refresh_from_db()
    assert before <= status.timestamp <= after


def test_deleting_a_job_deletes_only_its_own_statuses() -> None:
    doomed = Job.objects.create(name="doomed")
    kept = Job.objects.create(name="kept")
    JobStatus.objects.create(job=doomed, status_type=StatusType.PENDING)
    JobStatus.objects.create(job=doomed, status_type=StatusType.RUNNING)
    kept_status = JobStatus.objects.create(job=kept, status_type=StatusType.PENDING)

    doomed.delete()

    assert list(Job.objects.all()) == [kept]
    assert list(JobStatus.objects.all()) == [kept_status]


def test_migrations_match_the_models() -> None:
    # --check exits non-zero (SystemExit) when a model change has no migration.
    call_command("makemigrations", "--check", "--dry-run")

Phase 2 is built and verified; nothing is committed, it is ready for your review.

## Verification
- **`make test-backend`**: failed first with `No module named 'jobs.models'`, then 17 passed after the models and migration.
- **`make test`** (the gate): still passes after the Dockerfile and compose changes.
- **Schema in real Postgres** (throwaway stack): three check constraints, `bigint` ids, the FK and the `job_id` index are present, with no `ON DELETE` clause, as expected.
- **Raw SQL delete** of a job with statuses is refused with an FK error; nothing is orphaned.
- **Runtime image** has no pytest and still runs as `app`.
- **Cleanup**: no `job-dashboard` containers or volumes left behind.

## What was built
- **Models** ([models.py](backend/jobs/models.py)): one `StatusType` enum shared by `Job.current_status` and `JobStatus.status_type`, with the fields the brief lists.
- **Migration** ([0001_initial.py](backend/jobs/migrations/0001_initial.py)): generated in the container, not hand-written. A test fails if models and migrations drift.
- **Tests** ([test_models.py](backend/jobs/tests/test_models.py)): timestamps (clock patched, no sleeps), the `PENDING` default, the three constraints, the 255/256 name limit and the cascade.
- **Harness**: [requirements-dev.txt](backend/requirements-dev.txt), a `test` stage in [backend/Dockerfile](backend/Dockerfile), [pytest.ini](backend/pytest.ini), [docker-compose.backend-test.yml](docker-compose.backend-test.yml) and a `make test-backend` target in the [Makefile](Makefile).
- **[CLAUDE.md](CLAUDE.md)**: Phase 1 title cleaned, Phase 2 marked `[~]`, four decision rows added, manual check reworded, and notes added to Phases 3 and 4.

## Deferred (each has a `TODO` in `models.py`)
- **`current_status` is not database-enforced against the log.** Deferred because the only writers will be the Phase 3 services, in one transaction; the fix is a trigger or deriving it on read.
- **Cascade is done by Django, not the database.** Deferred because Django 5.2 cannot declare it; the fix is `ON DELETE CASCADE` on the constraint.
- **No `(job, -timestamp)` or `(current_status, -id)` index.** Deferred because there is no history view or filter yet and each index slows writes; the fix is to add each with its feature.

## Notes by analogy to your stack
- **Migrations** are Alembic's `revision --autogenerate`; here the test database is built from the migration file itself.
- **`TextChoices`** is like a SQLAlchemy `Enum`, but stored as a plain `varchar`; that is why the `CHECK` constraints exist.
- **Dockerfile stages** are like two images sharing a parent: `runtime` is last, so it stays the default.

The command that produces the migration is now in CLAUDE.md under Conventions. Read `0001_initial.py`, then:

make up
